subject: Materials Science
title: Space Shuttle Tiles
description: A short lesson to help you apply Space Shuttle Tiles.

hook.text: During re-entry, the Space Shuttle's belly hit 1,650°C. Ceramic tiles kept the crew alive.

buildup.text: Each tile was 90% air — silica fibers woven into an ultra-lightweight insulating block.

discovery.text: You could hold a tile's edge seconds after removing it from a 1,200°C oven — it insulated that well.

twist.text: The tiles were so fragile that a fingernail could gouge them — strength was sacrificed for lightness.

climax.text: Columbia's disaster in 2003 began when foam broke a tile, exposing aluminum to re-entry heat.

punchline.text: Those tiles traded toughness for the lightest heat shield ever made.

quiz.question: Why were Space Shuttle tiles so effective at insulating?
options: They were made of solid metal
They were 90% air, trapping heat in silica fiber
They absorbed heat by melting away
